newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa has some breathing problems.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa has some breathing problems.

text.p: Mother Teresa, in intensive care recovering from heart surgery, had some trouble breathing overnight and slept fitfully, but her general condition remained unchanged, doctors said on Friday.
"She had some breathing problems last night and her sleep was disturbed," Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in a regular update on her condition.
Last month, the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun had heart surgery to clear two blocked coronary arteries. She had similar surgery in 1991 in the United States and in 1993 at the Birla clinic.

On Wednesday, doctors gave her a mild electric shock to correct an irregular heart beat. Afterwards, they said the procedure, during which Mother Teresa remained conscious but under sedation, was a success.

But her recovery has been complicated by nagging bronchitis. Doctors have said they would like her to be back at her Missionaries of Charity religious order by Christmas, but that there is no assurance.
"Mother Teresa's condition remains (the) same after the cardioversion," the medical update said, adding that doctors were monitoring her heart closely.
The clinic said the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner had her morning tea at around 7 a.m. "She sat on a chair near her bed and said her prayers," it said.
The revered missionary has been pressing doctors to let her return to her religious order to resume her work with the sick and dying, for which she has been dubbed "Saint of the Gutters".
But doctors have cautioned that her recovery will be slow and she might never be as active as before.
